newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Gasoline actively bid, rebounds.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Gasoline actively bid, rebounds.

text.p: Gasoline prices rebounded as as aggressive buyers emerged to actively bid up despite weaker crude, traders said on Friday.
"Everybody is bidding, but there is no change fundamentally ... they are just supporting levels," said one trader.
Bids for two cargoes of 50,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded gasoline, started at $24.85 per barrel, fob Singapore, and improved to $25.25. On Thursday, a cargo was traded at $24.80.
A bid for a cargo of 92-octane unleaded gasoline was raised intraday from $24.50 to $24.90 while 97-octane bids rose from $25.90 to $26.50.
Some traders said levels were being supported prior to the closure of Taiwan's import tender January 28.
Some traders said Asian barrels were heading to the U.S. west coast, but they might be co-loaded cargoes as no shipping fixtures have been sighted to support the move.
A Yanbu cargo loading end-January was heard heading south to New Zealand.

The unscheduled shutdown of Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd (Ampol) 22,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) fluid catalytic cracker (FCC) due to regenerator problems at Kurnell from January 7 until the end of the month has not prompted any additional demand.
"We are moving mogas down from Brisbane which is running flat out," said a source.
Ampol will go-ahead with its plans to shut down for maintenance its other 23,000-bpd FCC located at Kurnell refinery, mid-February for three weeks, the company source said.
Naphtha edged up with February swaps up to $23.35/$23.60 from bids on Thursday at $23.30.
